_: Kill-check for the statement scanner in packages/store/src/statements.ts, written when the scanner was reviewed and its nine extracted closures were held to the README invariant. Each mutant breaks ONE property the scanner's own doc-comment claims, and names the single test that must notice. The killers were found empirically, not guessed: each mutant was applied, the owning test file was run with vitest's JSON reporter, and the failing test names were read off -- a killer that only *should* fail is exactly the false green this file exists to prevent. S1 is an intended survivor: the mutant is equivalent, so no test can kill it, and saying so is the point of the `why`.

mutants.why: The line is reached only from the `single`/`double`/`backtick` case, and `QUOTE_CLOSES` is a literal holding all three of those keys, so `.get` returns a string here every time and the fallback never fires -- a change no test can observe, and one no test should be written to catch. It is here so the run exercises the intended-survivor path and reports `held` rather than a false kill.
